methods.name: Bank FX purchase + SWIFT wire (documented China-source income)
methods.one_line: The default route: buy USD at your Chinese bank against proof of lawful current-account income, then wire it to your US account.
methods.who: A US citizen who is an overseas individual under the Chinese rules (passport holder) and whose RMB is lawful current-account income earned in China - salary, fees, rent, interest already taxed, pension paid from China.
methods.tax_note: No Chinese tax on the conversion. Chinese tax was due on the income when it arose. US: no tax on moving your own principal (§988(e)); reporting duties apply.
methods.ceiling: No annual facilitation quota applies to an overseas individual without a Chinese permanent-residence ID (S05). The USD 50,000/day figure is the ID-only processing threshold for remitting from an FX account, above which documents are required - it is not a prohibition (S02 Art.14).
pros: Cheapest lawful route in this study: the fixed fees are small relative to the balance.
Expressly contemplated by the rules for an overseas individual (S04 Art.59), and no purchase-application form is required of an overseas individual (S18).
Proceeds go straight into your own US account in USD; no offshore intermediary account needed.
cons: Requires a paper trail tying the RMB to a lawful China-source income event, including tax vouchers (S02 Art.13(1)).
Bank-level execution varies: the branch decides what documents are sufficient and may cap a single wire.
The spread is set commercially and is not published as a rule (S03 Art.27 sets only the exchange-rate regime).
docs: Passport
Chinese bank account statements showing the RMB balance
Evidence of the income source (employment contract, payslip, lease, interest statement)
Chinese tax payment certificates or withholding records
US bank details: account number, SWIFT/BIC, ABA routing number
methods.gap: Documentary cost (notarisation, translation, courier) is not quantified here because no official price list exists; it is flagged U05.

methods.name: Bank FX purchase + wire, drip-fed under the USD 50,000 annual quota
methods.one_line: What most people are told to do: spend the USD 50,000-per-person-per-year facilitation quota, year after year.
methods.who: A domestic individual, or an overseas individual whom the branch treats as quota-bound. It is the only personal route that is purely administrative, but it is slow.
methods.tax_note: Same as M01: no tax on the conversion itself. Repeated small conversions do not reduce tax, only fees and time.
methods.ceiling: USD 50,000 equivalent per person per year (S02 Art.2; S04 Art.54). A USD 400,000 balance therefore takes 8 calendar years.
pros: Least document-intensive per tranche, and the quota is a legal entitlement inside the annual amount.
Can be started immediately, online in many banks.
cons: Time: 8 years for USD 400,000, and the quota is per person per year, not per balance.
Eight wires means eight sets of fixed charges (cable, correspondent, receiving bank).
Buying FX for overseas house purchase, securities or life insurance is expressly prohibited (S06); filling in a false purpose is a false declaration.
Borrowing another person's quota to split a balance is expressly prohibited (S06; S01 Art.7).
docs: ID or passport
Completed Individual FX Purchase Application (required of domestic individuals, S04 Art.57)
methods.gap: The 8-year schedule assumes one person and no change in the quota, which the regulator may adjust (S02 Art.2).

methods.name: Emigration transfer (移民转移) - whole-balance route after you emigrate
methods.one_line: If you have given up Chinese household registration and settled abroad, SAFE can approve the transfer of your entire pre-emigration domestic property, released in three stages over two years.
methods.who: A natural person who has moved from mainland China to a foreign country (or HK/Macau) and holds proof of settlement abroad plus cancellation of Chinese household registration.
methods.tax_note: The tax certificate is a precondition, not a new tax: the transfer requires a tax payment certificate or a tax exemption document from the tax authority where the property is located (S07 Art.8(6)).
methods.ceiling: No amount ceiling is stated; approval is by SAFE (local branch up to RMB 500,000, SAFE head office above that - S07 Art.10). Release: up to half first, up to half of the remainder after one year, the rest after two years (S07 Art.6).
pros: Designed for exactly this problem: it moves a whole balance, not USD 50,000 a year.
The staged release is two years, not eight or more.
The bank must remit abroad directly to your own account - no cash stage (S07 Art.11).
cons: Requires that you have actually emigrated: police certificate cancelling household registration and proof of settlement abroad (S07 Art.8(4)).
SAFE approval required, with a full file: application form, property title documents, tax certificate, notarised translations (S07 Arts.8-9).
Property that cannot be shown to have a lawful source, or that is subject to litigation, is refused (S07 Art.12).
Three releases means three sets of bank charges.
docs: Written application explaining the source and realisation of the property
Completed emigrant property transfer applicant form and FX business application form
Passport plus police-issued cancellation of household registration
Proof of settlement abroad, issued or authenticated by a Chinese embassy or consulate
Property title documents (deed, sale contract, relocation compensation agreement)
Tax certificate or tax-paid voucher from the tax authority
Notarised translations of any foreign-language document
methods.gap: Notarisation, translation and agent fees are not quantified - no official price list (flag U05).

methods.name: Inheritance transfer (继承转移)
methods.one_line: A foreign citizen who has lawfully inherited property in China can apply to SAFE to realise it and remit the proceeds.
methods.who: A foreign citizen (or HK/Macau resident) who has inherited a mainland estate.
methods.tax_note: A tax certificate or tax-paid voucher from the tax authority where the estate is located is a required document (S07 Art.9(5)).
methods.ceiling: No amount ceiling stated. One application per deceased person, which may be remitted in one or several payments (S07 Art.6). The RB 500,000 approval threshold in Art.10 applies.
pros: Moves an inherited balance without the annual personal quota.
One application can cover the whole inheritance from one deceased person.
cons: Requires inheritance documentation, notarised where not already notarised (S07 Art.9).
The estate must be realised (sold/converted) before transfer.
SAFE approval; the tax certificate must come first.
docs: Written application describing the relationship and the source of the estate
FX business application form
Passport and proof of settlement abroad
Inheritance documents (will, grant, notarial certificate)
Deceased's title documents and the tax certificate
Notarised translations
methods.gap: Notarisation and translation costs are not quantified (flag U05).

methods.name: Sale proceeds of your own Chinese property (overseas individual)
methods.one_line: If you are an overseas individual selling a Chinese home you own, the proceeds can be purchased and remitted with SAFE approval.
methods.who: A foreign citizen who owns and sells domestic commercial property.
methods.tax_note: Chinese individual income tax applies to the *gain* on the transfer of assets at a flat 20% (S08 Arts.2(8), 3(3)). That tax is owed because the property was sold, not because the money moves. The tax certificate is a precondition to the transfer (S07 Art.8(6)).
methods.ceiling: SAFE approval required (S01 Art.22). No amount ceiling stated in the instrument.
pros: A defined statutory route for exactly this asset.
The 20% is a tax on the gain, so the effective rate on the whole balance is much lower than 20%.
cons: SAFE approval plus a tax clearance certificate before the bank will act.
Other Chinese taxes on a property transfer (for example VAT and deed tax) were not verified in this session and are therefore not quantified - flag U06.
Gain must be computed from the original cost basis, which requires the original purchase documents.
docs: Property title certificate and sale contract
Tax certificate or tax-paid voucher for the transfer
Passport and proof of the property being self-use as required
SAFE approval document
methods.gap: Chinese VAT/deed tax on the transfer, and the notarisation cost, are unverified (flags U05, U06).

methods.name: Remit USD you already hold (no conversion at all)
methods.one_line: If part of the balance is already in a foreign-currency savings account, there is nothing to convert - you only pay the wire.
methods.who: Anyone holding USD (or another convertible currency) in a Chinese FX savings account.
methods.tax_note: No Chinese tax and no conversion spread; only the transfer charges. US reporting still applies.
methods.ceiling: An overseas individual remitting from an FX savings account does so on valid ID (S02 Art.15). The USD 50,000/day threshold is the ID-only processing limit for a domestic individual (S02 Art.14).
pros: Zero FX spread - the single largest component of the cost disappears.
Minimal documentation for an overseas individual (S02 Art.15).
cons: Only works for the portion already held in foreign currency.
Correspondent and receiving-bank charges still apply.
docs: Passport
FX account statement
US bank details
methods.gap: Bank commission on an FX-account remittance is not verified against an official tariff (flag U01).

methods.name: RMB to Hong Kong, convert offshore (CNH), then wire to the US
methods.one_line: Move RMB to your own Hong Kong account, convert it there at offshore rates, and wire USD onward.
methods.who: Someone who already holds, or can open, a Hong Kong account in the same name and can satisfy the mainland bank that the RMB remittance is a permitted current-account payment.
methods.tax_note: No Chinese tax on the conversion; the same tax-on-the-event analysis applies. The offshore spread is a commercial price, not a rule.
methods.ceiling: Not established by any instrument reviewed. Whether a mainland bank will remit RMB to a same-name Hong Kong account for an individual, and on what documents, is a bank and branch question - flag U02.
pros: Offshore CNH spreads can be narrower than onshore retail spreads.
Once the money is offshore, later movement is outside Chinese FX control.
cons: Adds an intermediary bank, an intermediary jurisdiction and a second set of charges.
Requires a Hong Kong account and, in practice, proof of the same-name link.
The onshore leg is still a cross-border RMB payment subject to the same authenticity rules (S03 Art.12).
Two conversions or one conversion plus a wire means more spread, not less, unless the offshore spread is materially tighter - which is unverified here.
docs: Passport and Hong Kong account proof
Same-name evidence
Source-of-funds documents for the mainland bank
methods.gap: No official source located for the onshore RMB remittance fee, the offshore CNH spread, or the Hong Kong wire fee; the cost table is therefore left blank and flagged (U02, U03).

methods.name: Withdraw RMB abroad with a Chinese bank card, then convert
methods.one_line: Use the card at an overseas ATM, then convert the cash locally.
methods.who: Anyone with a mainland-issued RMB or foreign-currency card.
methods.tax_note: No Chinese tax on the conversion; the limits are prudential, not fiscal.
methods.ceiling: RMB 100,000 equivalent per person per calendar year across all domestic cards, and RMB 10,000 per card per day (S15).
pros: No SAFE application, no bank appointment.
Works today, in small amounts.
cons: Structurally slow: about USD 14,942 a year at the board rate, so USD 400,000 needs 27 card-years.
Exceeding the annual cap suspends overseas cash withdrawal for the rest of that year and the next (S15).
Cash is the least safe and most expensive form of value to move, and carrying more than USD 10,000 into the US triggers a separate US reporting obligation.
ATM fees and the local conversion spread are set by the ATM operator and the card network - not verified here (flag U04).
docs: Chinese bank card
Passport
methods.gap: ATM and conversion fees are unverified (U04); the US cash-declaration penalty was not verified in this session and is flagged.

methods.name: Carry foreign cash out of China
methods.one_line: Physical carriage, inside the customs permit thresholds.
methods.who: Anyone prepared to travel repeatedly with cash.
methods.tax_note: No tax on the conversion; the exposure is customs and FX-control based.
methods.ceiling: Up to USD 5,000 without a permit; USD 5,000-10,000 with a bank-issued carrying permit; above USD 10,000 a SAFE-issued permit is required in principle (S14).
pros: No SAFE approval for amounts up to USD 5,000 per exit.
The cash and transfer rates at the bank are identical on the sample board (S09), so there is no extra cash spread at that bank on that day.
cons: USD 400,000 would need 40 permitted trips at USD 10,000 each.
Illegal carriage of FX across the border carries a warning and a fine of up to 20% of the amount (S03 Art.42).
Physical loss and theft risk is total, not proportional.
Entering the US with more than USD 10,000 in cash triggers a separate US declaration obligation.
docs: Passport
Bank carrying permit (USD 5,000-10,000)
SAFE permit (above USD 10,000 in principle)
methods.gap: Travel, insurance and safe-custody costs are not quantified; no official tariff exists (flag U05).

methods.name: Company dividend remittance (if the money belongs to a company you own)
methods.one_line: If the balance sits in a Chinese company rather than your own name, a profit distribution is the normal route - and it carries withholding tax on the profit.
methods.who: A foreign investor in a Chinese company with distributable after-tax profits.
methods.tax_note: Dividends paid out of China carry enterprise income tax withheld at source. The statutory rate and the reduced rate for a non-resident enterprise were not verified against the primary text in this session, so no rate is stated here (flag U07).
methods.ceiling: No individual quota applies, because the money is corporate. Profit must be after-tax and the distribution must follow company law and the articles.
pros: Not constrained by the personal USD 50,000 quota.
A well-trodden institutional process with banks that handle FDI accounts daily.
cons: Withholding tax is a real cost on the profit distributed - it is a tax on the profit, not on the transfer.
Requires audited accounts, a tax clearance and a board resolution.
Only usable if the money genuinely belongs to the company; treating personal money as corporate is a compliance problem.
docs: Board resolution and profit distribution plan
Audited financial statements
Tax clearance / withholding receipts
FDI registration documents
methods.gap: The Chinese withholding rate and the treaty rate were not verified in this session (U07).

methods.name: Liquidation or capital reduction of a foreign-invested enterprise
methods.one_line: An express statutory entitlement: after a foreign-invested enterprise is lawfully terminated, liquidated and taxed, the foreign investor's RMB may be purchased and remitted.
methods.who: The foreign investor of a company that is being wound up or reduced in capital.
methods.tax_note: Liquidation tax is settled before the remittance; the article makes tax payment part of the sequence, not a levy on the transfer (S03 Art.22).
methods.ceiling: No amount ceiling in the article; the constraint is the liquidation and tax process.
pros: Written into a State Council regulation - the clearest statutory language of any whole-balance route.
Moves the whole remaining capital, not a quota-sized slice.
cons: Terminating or reducing a company is a major corporate act with its own legal and tax cost.
Only relevant if the money is genuinely corporate capital.
docs: Liquidation approval and filings
Liquidation tax clearance
Capital account registration documents
methods.gap: Liquidation costs and tax are company-specific and are not quantified.

methods.name: Splitting a balance across relatives' quotas (分拆结售汇)
methods.one_line: The 'ants moving house' pattern. Prohibited, monitored, and the most common way a manageable problem becomes a penalty.
methods.tax_note: No tax analysis applies, because the route itself is unlawful.
cons: Expressly prohibited: no borrowing or lending of quota, no splitting to evade the limits (S01 Art.7; S06).
Evasion of FX control carries a fine of up to 30% of the amount, and 30% to 100% in serious cases (S03 Art.39).
Being placed on the watch list suspends the facilitation quota in practice, which removes the lawful route you were trying to preserve.
methods.gap: The artificial split makes every participant's declaration false; all of them bear the exposure.

methods.name: Underground banks and private FX dealing (地下钱庄)
methods.one_line: A counterparty takes RMB in China and pays USD abroad, netting the two sides. Criminal, and the counterparty risk is total.
methods.ceiling: Private, disguised or brokered FX trading is penalised at up to 30% of the amount, and 30%-100% in serious cases, with criminal liability where constituted (S03 Art.45).
cons: The funds you receive abroad are the proceeds of an unlawful arrangement and can be traced and frozen.
Fines of up to 30%, and 30%-100% in serious cases, plus criminal exposure (S03 Art.45).
There is no contract you can enforce if the counterparty keeps the money.
methods.gap: Loss of the entire principal to the counterparty is a real risk not captured by any fine range.

methods.name: False documents and false purpose declarations (骗购外汇)
methods.one_line: Inventing a study, travel or trade purpose, or using a fabricated invoice, to obtain FX.
methods.ceiling: Illegal FX arbitrage is fined at up to 30% of the amount, and 30%-100% in serious cases (S03 Art.40). Submitting untrue documents attracts a separate individual fine of up to RMB 50,000 (S03 Art.48).
cons: Every remittance rests on a genuine transaction basis (S03 Art.12); a false declaration is a false statement to the bank and the regulator.
Two separate penalty provisions can apply (S03 Arts.40, 48).
The bank also faces penalties for weak review, so scrutiny is structural, not incidental.

methods.name: Converting through crypto or a stablecoin (USDT)
methods.one_line: Frequently proposed online. In China it is an illegal financial activity, and the offshore exchange serving you is itself acting unlawfully.
methods.who: Not available lawfully to anyone in mainland China.
methods.ceiling: Exchange between legal tender and virtual currency is an illegal financial activity to be strictly prohibited (S16 Arts.1(2)-(3)); it may also be treated as disguised FX trading (S03 Art.45).
cons: Virtual currency has no legal-tender status and may not circulate as currency in China (S16 Art.1(1)).
Offshore exchanges serving mainland residents through the internet are committing an illegal financial activity (S16 Art.1(3)).
Banks and payment institutions may not process the transfers, so the on-ramp is itself a person willing to break the rules (S16 Art.9).
In the US, a receipt treated as a gift or a sale has its own reporting consequences.

methods.name: Carrying out more cash than the permit allows, or not declaring it
methods.one_line: The cash route stops being lawful the moment the permit threshold is crossed.
methods.ceiling: Illegal carriage of FX across the border: warning plus a fine of up to 20% of the amount (S03 Art.42).
cons: A 20% fine is roughly 80 times the cost of wiring the same money lawfully (see the cost tables).
Cash can be seized at the border.
A separate US declaration obligation applies on entry.

methods.name: Buying FX for overseas property, securities or life insurance
methods.one_line: The purpose restriction is the one most likely to catch an otherwise lawful transfer.
methods.who: Not available lawfully to anyone purchasing FX as a domestic individual.
methods.ceiling: Unauthorised change of use of FX or settled funds: fine of up to 30%, and 30%-100% in serious cases (S03 Art.44).
cons: Expressly listed among the six prohibitions for a domestic individual's purchase (S06).
Capital-account convertibility is not open, so there is no alternative paperwork that makes it lawful (S01 Art.3).

methods.name: Wise, Revolut, Payoneer or similar transfer apps
methods.one_line: Popular in other corridors; not a route out of a mainland bank account.
methods.who: Not available for mainland-China personal CNY outbound transfers as far as this research found.
cons: No official source was located showing that these services can fund a personal CNY outbound transfer from a mainland account.
Business and e-commerce corridors are a different product and are not a substitute for personal repatriation.
methods.gap: Unverified: no official confirmation either way. Flag U08.

methods.name: QDII / QDLP funds
methods.one_line: An investment product, not a repatriation route: you buy a fund onshore with RMB; you do not get USD into your US account.
methods.tax_note: Not applicable: the money does not leave your ownership.
pros: A lawful way for a domestic individual to obtain offshore exposure.
cons: Does not move money out of China or into your US account.
Redemption returns RMB onshore.

S01.title: 个人外汇管理办法 (Measures for the Administration of Individual Foreign Exchange)
S01.inspected: Full text retrieved and read: Arts. 3, 7, 9, 13, 16-23, 26, 30-35, 37.
supports: Art.3: current-account individual FX is managed on the convertibility principle; capital-account FX follows the convertibility process (i.e. is not automatically convertible).
Art.7: splitting transactions to evade quota supervision, and false commercial documents, are prohibited.
Art.9: annual total-amount management applies to individual FX settlement and to FX purchase by a *domestic* individual.
Art.13: an overseas individual may purchase FX and remit lawful current-account RMB income earned in China, on ID and supporting documents.
Art.22: an overseas individual selling domestic commercial property may purchase FX and remit the proceeds with SAFE approval.
Art.26: outward transfer of an overseas individual's lawful domestic property follows the property-transfer rules.
Art.37(2): an overseas individual is a foreign citizen holding a passport (or HK/Macau/Taiwan resident).

S02.short: Detailed Rules on Individual FX (2007, as amended)
S02.title: 个人外汇管理办法实施细则 (Detailed Rules for the Implementation of the Measures for the Administration of Individual Foreign Exchange), as amended
S02.inspected: Full text retrieved and read, including the two amendment notes at the foot of the page.
supports: Art.2: the annual total amount is USD 50,000 equivalent per person per year, applied to individual FX settlement and to FX purchase by a domestic individual.
Art.13(1): an overseas individual purchasing FX against lawful current-account RMB income earned in China provides ID and transaction evidence *including tax vouchers*.
Art.13(2): reconversion of unused RMB requires the original exchange memo, valid for 24 months.
Art.14: a domestic individual remitting FX abroad for current-account purposes on ID alone is limited to USD 50,000/day; above that, authenticity documents are required.
Art.15: an overseas individual remitting from an FX savings account does so on valid ID.
Art.20: emigration and inheritance transfers are handled under the 2004 Interim Measures.
Art.21: an overseas individual's purchase/sale of domestic commercial property is handled under the property-FX rules.
Art.30: cash withdrawal above USD 10,000/day requires prior SAFE filing.
Art.39 was repealed by 汇发〔2023〕8号 (noted on the page).

S03.title: 中华人民共和国外汇管理条例 (Regulation on the Foreign Exchange System of the PRC)
S03.inspected: Full text retrieved and read: Arts. 5, 6, 8, 12, 14, 15, 22, 27, 39-48, 52.
supports: Art.5: the State does not restrict current-account international payments and transfers.
Art.12: current-account FX receipts and payments must rest on a genuine, lawful transaction basis.
Art.15: the limits for carrying and declaring foreign cash across the border are set by the FX authority.
Art.22 para.2: RMB belonging to the foreign investor of a lawfully terminated foreign-invested enterprise may be purchased and remitted after liquidation and tax payment.
Art.27: the RMB exchange rate is a managed float based on market supply and demand.
Art.39: evasion of FX control (逃汇) - fine of up to 30% of the evaded amount; serious cases 30% up to the same amount.
Art.40: illegal arbitrage of FX (非法套汇, including purchase on false documents) - same 0-30% / 30%-100% range.
Art.42: illegal carriage of FX across the border - warning and a fine of up to 20% of the amount.
Art.44: unauthorised change of use of FX or of settled FX - 0-30%, serious 30%-100%.
Art.45: private or disguised trading of FX - 0-30%, serious 30%-100%; criminal liability if constituted.
Art.48: failure to submit valid documents or submission of untrue documents - individual fine up to RMB 50,000.
Art.52(2): 'domestic individual' includes a Chinese citizen *and a foreigner who has continuously resided in China for one year or more*.

S04.title: 经常项目外汇业务指引（2020年版） (Guide to Current-Account Foreign Exchange Business, 2020 edition)
S04.inspected: State Council Gazette text retrieved in parts: Arts. 54-59 (from the gazette and the SAFE Q&A at S05), 64, 86-89, 178.
supports: Art.54: individual FX settlement and FX purchase by a domestic individual are subject to an annual facilitation quota of USD 50,000 equivalent per person per year.
Art.57: a domestic individual purchasing FX must complete the Individual FX Purchase Application and bears legal responsibility for it.
Art.58: an overseas individual settling FX provides ID and evidence of the use of funds; settlements above USD 50,000 must be paid directly to the counterparty's onshore RMB account.

Art.59: an overseas individual's lawful current-account RMB income earned in China may be purchased with ID and source-of-funds evidence (including tax vouchers); the annual facilitation quota applies only to holders of a Foreigner's Permanent Residence ID.

Arts.86-89: cash rules - withdrawal or deposit of up to USD 10,000/day on ID; carrying cash in above USD 5,000 requires written customs declaration; carrying out USD 5,000-10,000 requires a bank-issued carrying permit; above USD 10,000 requires a SAFE-issued permit.
Art.178: for individual settlement/purchase above USD 50,000, authenticity review of documents applies.

S05.title: 2024年经常项目外汇政策问答案例（九） - 境外个人是否享受年度便利化额度购汇？
supports: Answers directly that an overseas individual purchasing FX against lawful current-account RMB income earned in China does so under Art.59 with ID and source-of-funds evidence including tax vouchers; only an overseas individual holding a Foreigner's Permanent Residence ID is subject to the annual facilitation quota.

S06.short: SAFE Tianjin Q&A (2017) - the six prohibitions
S06.title: 2017年个人外汇管理问题解答（二）
supports: Lists the six prohibitions a domestic individual accepts when purchasing FX, including: no overseas house purchase, securities investment or life/return-of-premium insurance with purchased FX; no lending or borrowing of another person's facilitation quota; no splitting; no money laundering, tax evasion or underground-bank dealings.

S07.short: Interim Measures on Outward Transfer of Personal Property (2004)
S07.title: 个人财产对外转移售付汇管理暂行办法
S07.doc: 中国人民银行公告〔2004〕第16号
S07.inspected: Full text retrieved and read: Arts. 2-16.
supports: Art.2: emigration transfer (移民转移) and inheritance transfer (继承转移) are the two forms of outward transfer of personal property.

Art.6: an emigration transfer must be applied for once for the whole amount and is released in stages - first no more than half, a further no more than half of the remainder after one year, the balance after two years; amounts up to RMB 200,000 may be released at once.

Art.8(4): the applicant must produce the police-issued cancellation of Chinese household registration (户籍注销证明) and proof of settlement abroad; Art.8(6): a tax certificate or tax-paid voucher from the tax authority.
Art.10: applications up to RMB 500,000 are approved by the local SAFE branch; above that, by SAFE head office.
Art.11: the bank must remit directly to the applicant's own account abroad; cash withdrawal onshore is not permitted.
Art.12: property that cannot be shown to have a lawful source is not accepted.

S08.short: Individual Income Tax Law (official English text)
S08.title: Individual Income Tax Law of the People's Republic of China
S08.inspected: Full text retrieved and read: Arts. 1, 2, 3, 4, 6.
supports: Art.1: a resident individual (domiciled, or 183+ days in a tax year) is taxed on income from within and outside China; a non-resident on China-source income.

Art.2: tax is imposed on nine enumerated categories of income (wages; personal services; author's remuneration; royalties; business operation; interest, dividends and bonuses; leasing of assets; transfer of assets; incidental income). The exchange of one currency for another is not one of them.
Art.3: comprehensive income 3%-45%; business income 5%-35%; interest, dividends, leasing, transfer of assets and incidental income a flat 20%.

S09.short: Bank of China FX rate board
S09.title: 中国银行外汇牌价 (Bank of China foreign exchange rate board)
S09.doc: Rates quoted in CNY per 100 units of foreign currency
S09.inspected: Page retrieved. USD row read: 现汇买入价 666.48 / 现钞买入价 666.48 / 现汇卖出价 669.29 / 现钞卖出价 669.29 / 中行折算价 671.68.
supports: USD cash-buying and transfer-buying rates are identical on this board, and the cash-selling and transfer-selling rates are identical (666.48 buy / 669.29 sell CNY per 100 USD).
The bank's own buy/sell gap is (669.29-666.48)/669.29 = 0.4199% of the selling rate.
The rate at which a customer obtains USD is 669.29 CNY per 100 USD, i.e. 6.6929 CNY per USD.

S10.short: IRS - Report of Foreign Bank and Financial Accounts (FBAR)
S10.title: Report of Foreign Bank and Financial Accounts (FBAR)
supports: A US person must file an FBAR where the aggregate value of foreign financial accounts exceeded USD 10,000 at any time in the calendar year.
Whether the account produced taxable income has no effect on the filing obligation.
Civil penalty maximums are set in Title 31 and adjusted annually for inflation.

S11.short: IRS - Gifts from a foreign person
S11.title: Gifts from foreign person (International tax gap series)
supports: A US person who receives gifts or bequests from a nonresident alien exceeding USD 100,000 in aggregate during the tax year must report them on Part IV of Form 3520.
A foreign gift is excluded from gross income; the obligation is reporting, not tax on the receipt.

S12.title: 26 U.S.C. §988 - Treatment of certain foreign currency transactions
S12.inspected: Section text retrieved and read, including subsection (e).
supports: §988(a): foreign-currency gain or loss on a §988 transaction is computed separately and treated as ordinary income or loss.
§988(c)(1)(C): a disposition of non-functional currency is a §988 transaction.
§988(e)(1): the section does not apply to a §988 transaction entered into by an individual which is a personal transaction.
§988(e)(2): on a personal transaction, no gain is recognised by reason of exchange-rate movement - but the exclusion does not apply if the gain would exceed USD 200.
§988(e)(3): 'personal transaction' means a transaction of an individual other than one with expenses meeting §162 or §212 (business/investment).

S13.title: Foreign Tax Credit
supports: A credit or deduction may be available for foreign income taxes imposed on income that is also subject to US tax; the credit is claimed on Form 1116.
The credit cannot exceed the US tax on the same income, and no credit is available for taxes on income excluded under the foreign earned income exclusion.

S14.short: Rules on carrying foreign cash across the border (2003)
S14.title: 携带外币现钞出入境管理暂行办法
S14.issuer: SAFE and General Administration of Customs
S14.inspected: Ministry of Commerce reprint of the joint SAFE/Customs notice retrieved and read (Arts. 2-10).
supports: Carrying out up to USD 5,000 equivalent needs no carrying permit; USD 5,000-10,000 needs a bank-issued permit; above USD 10,000 a SAFE-issued permit is required in principle.
Carrying in more than USD 5,000 equivalent must be declared in writing to Customs.
A bank may issue a permit only up to the amount of the deposit certificate or the amount of FX purchased, and each permit may not exceed USD 10,000.

S15.short: Notice on overseas ATM cash withdrawals (2017)
S15.title: 国家外汇管理局关于规范银行卡境外大额提取现金交易的通知
S15.inspected: Official SAFE page including the notice text, retrieved via the SAFE site search index; the same text was cross-read in SAFE's press release at m.safe.gov.cn/safe/2017/1230/12696.html.
supports: All of one person's domestic-bank cards together may withdraw no more than the equivalent of RMB 100,000 in cash outside mainland China per calendar year.
Each card is limited to the equivalent of RMB 10,000 per day, for both RMB and foreign-currency cards.
Exceeding the annual limit suspends overseas cash withdrawal for that year and the next; borrowing or lending cards to circumvent the limit is prohibited.

S16.title: 关于进一步防范和处置虚拟货币交易炒作风险的通知
supports: Virtual currency has no legal-tender status and may not circulate as currency in the market.
Exchange between legal tender and virtual currency, and virtual-currency business activity generally, is an illegal financial activity to be strictly prohibited and suppressed.
Offshore virtual-currency exchanges serving residents of mainland China through the internet commit an illegal financial activity.
Financial institutions and non-bank payment institutions may not provide account, transfer or settlement services for virtual-currency activity.

S17.short: Bank of America personal fee schedule
S17.title: Bank of America Advantage Relationship Banking - Personal Schedule of Fees extract
S17.inspected: Fee-schedule extract read; the incoming international wire line states USD 15.00 per incoming international wire transfer, with a note that other fees may also apply, including fees charged by the recipient's institution.
supports: An incoming international wire at this US bank costs USD 15.00 per transfer on the standard tier.
The bank itself warns that correspondent and other fees may also apply.

S18.short: SAFE Xiamen - individual FX service guide (PDF)
S18.title: 国家外汇管理局厦门市分局个人外汇业务服务小贴士
S18.inspected: PDF retrieved through the SAFE site search index; the individual-FX chapter was read.
supports: An overseas individual purchasing FX does not complete the Individual FX Purchase Application form (境外个人购汇无需填写《个人购汇申请书》).
The six prohibitions attach to the domestic individual's purchase, and are set out in the same guide.

S19.title: Publication 54, Tax Guide for U.S. Citizens and Resident Aliens Abroad
S19.inspected: Publication landing page and scope statement retrieved; the worldwide-income rule is stated there and in the IIT/FBAR material cited separately.
supports: US citizens and resident aliens are taxed on worldwide income, and must report foreign-source income on their US return.

flags.topic: Chinese bank remittance commission and cable charge
flags.detail: The 0.10% commission with a CNY 50 floor and a CNY 260 cap, plus a CNY 150 cable charge, is stated consistently across secondary sources but no official bank tariff page could be retrieved this session. Used as ASSUMPTION A2 and stress-tested.
flags.impact: If the real tariff is higher, every bank-wire total rises by the difference; the ranking of routes does not change because all bank routes use the same tariff.

flags.detail: No regulator or bank publishes a fixed correspondent deduction. USD 25 per transfer is used as ASSUMPTION A3 and is not verified. The receiving bank itself warns that other banks' fees may apply (S17).
flags.impact: Each transfer could be USD 10-50 higher or lower; the effect on the percentage is largest at USD 10,000.

flags.topic: Offshore CNH spread and Hong Kong wire fees (M07)
flags.detail: No official retail CNH spread and no Hong Kong bank tariff were located this session, so M07's cost table is left blank rather than estimated.
flags.impact: M07 cannot be ranked against M01 on the numbers. That is itself a finding: the popular 'route it through Hong Kong' advice is not supported by any price this research could verify.

flags.topic: Overseas ATM fees and cash conversion spread (M08)
flags.detail: The regulatory limits are verified (S15), but the fees charged by overseas ATM operators and card networks are not.
flags.impact: M08's cost column is blank; its time cost is quantified from the verified limits.

flags.topic: Notarisation, translation, courier and travel costs
flags.detail: Documentary costs for the property, emigration and inheritance routes are real but are not set by any official price list.
flags.impact: M03, M04, M05 and M09 totals exclude these costs and are therefore a floor, not a full cost.

flags.topic: Non-IIT taxes on a Chinese property sale
flags.detail: VAT, deed tax and any surcharges on the sale of a Chinese property were not verified in this session. Only the 20% IIT on the gain is quantified (S08).
flags.impact: The total cost of the property route is understated by an amount that could be material.

flags.topic: Chinese withholding rate on company dividends
flags.detail: The statutory and treaty rates for dividends paid to a non-resident enterprise were not verified against primary text in this session, so M10 states no rate.
flags.impact: M10's tax cost is blank. The route's existence and structure are verified (S03 Art.22).

flags.detail: Whether Wise, Revolut, Payoneer or similar can fund a personal CNY outbound transfer from a mainland account was not confirmed either way by an official source.
flags.impact: Listed as not available rather than as a route; treat any marketing claim to the contrary with suspicion.

flags.topic: Definitional conflict: who is a 'domestic individual'
flags.detail: The 2008 Regulation defines a domestic individual to include a foreigner who has resided in China for one year or more (S03 Art.52(2)), while the 2006 Measures define an overseas individual by passport (S01 Art.37(2)); S05 applies the no-quota treatment on the basis of the permanent-residence ID. The instruments are not obviously aligned.
flags.impact: This is the single most consequential ambiguity in the analysis: it decides whether M01's no-quota treatment or M02's eight-year drip applies. Ask the branch, in writing, which basis it applies.

flags.detail: Banks may cap a single outward remittance or require the balance to be split across several wires regardless of the documented route. No bank's internal limit was verified.
flags.impact: Each extra wire adds a set of fixed charges (cable + correspondent + receiving), which is quantified in the per-transfer columns.

flags.detail: The obligation to declare more than USD 10,000 in cash entering the US is well known but the penalty provision was not verified in this session.
flags.impact: No number is stated for it; the China-side 20% carriage fine is verified and quantified (S03 Art.42).

flags.detail: The exchange rate and the fee schedules are dated: the BOC board is 2026-11-09 05:30 Beijing time (S09) and the US fee schedule is the version published on the bank's site on the retrieval date (S17). Both will change.
flags.impact: Re-capture the rate on the day of the transaction; the site states its capture date on every page that uses it.

tax.note: The Individual Income Tax Law taxes nine enumerated categories of income (S08 Art.2). Exchanging one currency for another is not among them, and no FX instrument in this register imposes a conversion levy; the Regulation only establishes a managed floating rate (S03 Art.27).
Owed when the salary is paid, whether or not the money ever leaves China.

tax.event: Interest, dividends, leasing, transfer of assets, incidental income
tax.note: This is the rate that applies to a property gain. It is a tax on the gain, not on the remittance.

tax.event: Property transfer - tax certificate before remittance
tax.note: Both the emigration and the inheritance route require a tax certificate or tax-paid voucher from the tax authority as a document in the file.
On a personal transaction, no gain is recognised by reason of exchange-rate movement, unless the gain would exceed USD 200 (S12 §988(e)(2)). A transfer of your own after-tax money is not income.

tax.event: Worldwide income of a US citizen
tax.rate: Ordinary rates on the income, when earned
tax.note: A US citizen is taxed on worldwide income. The Chinese income was reportable when it arose; moving it later does not create a second tax event.

tax.event: Foreign tax already paid on the same income
tax.rate: Credit, limited to the US tax on that income
tax.note: Claimed on Form 1116; a credit is not available for tax on income excluded under the foreign earned income exclusion.

tax.rate: FBAR if aggregate > USD 10,000 at any time
tax.note: The filing duty does not depend on whether the account produced income.

tax.event: Large gift or bequest from a foreign person
tax.rate: Form 3520 Part IV if > USD 100,000 in the year
tax.note: The gift is excluded from gross income; the obligation is to report.

tax.event: Chinese withholding on a company dividend
tax.note: Enterprise income tax is withheld on dividends paid to a non-resident enterprise. The statutory and reduced rates were not verified against primary text here, so no number is stated. Flag U07.

penalties.route: Evasion of FX control (逃汇), including splitting to move a balance
penalties.fine: Up to 30% of the amount; 30%-100% if serious

penalties.route: Illegal FX arbitrage (非法套汇), including purchase on false documents
penalties.fine: Up to 30% of the amount; 30%-100% if serious

penalties.route: Unauthorised change of use of FX or of settled funds
penalties.fine: Up to 30% of the amount; 30%-100% if serious

penalties.route: Private, disguised or brokered FX trading (underground banks)
penalties.fine: Up to 30% of the amount; 30%-100% if serious

penalties.route: Illegal carriage of FX across the border
penalties.fine: Warning and up to 20% of the amount

penalties.route: Untrue documents or failure to submit valid documents

penalties.fine: Illegal financial activity: prohibited and suppressed; no penalty figure stated in the notice
penalties.criminal: Yes, where a crime is constituted

penalties.fine: Greater of USD 100,000 (inflation-adjusted) or 50% of the account balance at the time of the violation, per violation
penalties.criminal: Yes, under 31 U.S.C. §5322 where the tests are met
